quotes.text: MobilePay is a single-use card wallet payment method used in Denmark and Finland.
A partial capture is final: Stripe releases the uncaptured remainder, and you can’t make a second capture for it.
MobilePay doesn’t impose a single payment-method-specific refund deadline.
Returning doesn't by itself prove that the payment succeeded.
For Connect direct charges, Stripe uses the connected account’s descriptor.

old_evidence.text: MobilePay supports full and partial refunds.

findings: November remains a substantive product overview, not a selector. It documents the single-use underlying card wallet for DK/FI buyers, DKK/EUR/NOK/SEK, immediate confirmation versus standard payout, and the same 29 listed merchant locations as May (new lines 9-22, 51-64; old lines 8-36, 54-86). Source line 17 and wallet concept line 219 miscount the locations as 30. The minimum depends on settlement currency after conversion; 2.50 DKK illustrates DKK settlement only.

November adds explicit capture limits, operational refund/dispute details, an explicit Capabilities API request path for connected accounts without full Dashboard access, a product/API support matrix, and descriptor rules. Source lines 13-29 retain correct central claims but omit important conditions and rely on stale undated shorthand. See new lines 66-151, 203-213 against old lines 30-52, 102-137. The active-state check is retained from May: full-Dashboard connected accounts could enable in Payment methods, and Accounts API or account webhooks expose `capabilities.mobilepay_payments` (old lines 125-129; new lines 149-151). The November matrix supports the Payment Element and excludes Express Checkout Element and Payment Method Messaging Element (new lines 124-132).

The November statement descriptor uses the standard card suffix path with a 22-character complete descriptor and issuer display variation. Full `statement_descriptor` follows separate rules/fallback. For direct Connect charges the connected account supplies it, while destination charges use the platform unless `on_behalf_of` is set (new lines 203-207). This is separate from May's connected-account app/checkout naming (old lines 125-129).
Wiki index line 7 routes to Stripe index lines 384-385 and 406-407, and wallet concept lines 217-235 and 414-415. Those routes need reciprocal dated capture labels.
substantive_changes: New lines 18-64 add explicit merchant/platform and B2B/B2C listings, a prohibited MCC table and settlement-currency minimum. The May list of eight plain-language categories (old lines 162-175) was reorganized into named categories plus MCCs. An omitted old label does not establish relaxation.

New lines 66-92 explicitly support final partial capture with release of the remainder, disallow multicapture and overcapture, and list unsupported authorization variants. Old overview lines 46-48 only said manual capture is supported. Separate May acceptance evidence gives an opposing full-only statement for its documented manual-capture flows.

New lines 94-122 add card-network and regional refund deadlines, conditional cancellation, reversals, typically 5–10 business days depending on issuer, status/event handling, and issuer-decided card disputes with response deadlines. Old lines 131-137 established cumulative refund amount and standard card dispute treatment.

New lines 124-151 add an explicit product/API matrix and request procedure for connected accounts without full Dashboard access. Checkout Sessions are recommended; PaymentIntents are supported but `setup_future_usage`, SetupIntents and off-session use are unsupported. Platform/account support does not make a connected account's capability active. The explicit Capabilities API request is newly stated in this overview; the active-state check and full-Dashboard settings path are historical (old lines 125-129). The UI matrix supports the Payment Element and excludes Express Checkout Element and Payment Method Messaging Element.

New lines 163-175 narrow the Dankort explanation to using Visa for Visa/Dankort and qualify the monthly fee for applicable active Danish merchants of record, with inactivity/offboarding and negotiated/platform variation. New lines 195-207 explicitly qualify return outcome and give descriptor and charge-type rules.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Dated May evidence includes DK/FI buyers and four presentment currencies, immediate notification and separate standard payout, mobile redirect and desktop phone/push, Connect direct/destination/separate charges and transfers, and underlying card refunds/disputes (old lines 8-52, 88-141). November omission of separate-charges detail does not prove withdrawal.

May 3DS by country/card network estimates, 35 DKK amount and 250×250 branding recommendation remain dated (old lines 143-160, 183-214). November describes conditional 3DS, no merchant forcing and liability shift only when authentication occurred, without reattesting the rates (new lines 153-159).

May manual-capture route sections document `payment_intent_data.capture_method` on Checkout Sessions versus `capture_method` when creating a PaymentIntent, `requires_capture` after authorization and associated capturable event. The five-minute `requires_action` authentication rule is separate from capture timing (raw/stripe-mobilepay-accept-payment-2025.md:155-218, 776-827, 1027-1078). Keep May integration/API scope separate from the new overview.
conflicts: May 7 acceptance Checkout, Elements and Direct API sections say full-amount manual capture only (raw/stripe-mobilepay-accept-payment-2025.md:194, 804, 1055). November 7 product overview says partial capture is final, releases the uncaptured remainder and disallows later capture or overcapture (new lines 76-92). Preserve the dated conflict reciprocally in product/acceptance source routes and wallet concept. The November acceptance selector links six variants (raw/stripe-payments-mobilepay-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md:9-19) without their bodies. Neither its links nor the overview establish exact availability by API revision, SDK, platform, route, or account, and `amount_to_capture` in a full-amount May example does not prove earlier partial capture.

Source line 17 and wallet concept line 219 state 30 merchant countries; both pinned captures list 29 (old lines 58-86 and new lines 19 and 53). Source lines 13, 25 and 27-33 and wallet concept lines 225-233 need capture dates and the November fee, Dankort and MCC qualifications; omissions do not prove fee removal, price continuity, or category eligibility.
unresolved_questions: The captures do not resolve exactly which integration/API versions or merchants receive partial capture or when the change became available. The linked November acceptance variants were not read beyond their selector.

findings: Preserve both overview captures. Correct the 29-location count. Surface final partial capture with remaining authorization release, and preserve refund/dispute state, settlement-currency minimum, eligibility/active capability, product matrix, descriptor rules and dated limitations with direct locators.

Keep the front-end Dashboard Payment methods enablement requirement (old lines 102-115 and new lines 209-213) and the separate connected-account paths. May documents full-Dashboard Payment methods and an active `capabilities.mobilepay_payments` check via Accounts API or webhooks (old lines 125-129); November retains the active check and explicitly directs a Capabilities API request without full Dashboard access (new lines 149-151). In November the Payment Element is supported, while Express Checkout Element and Payment Method Messaging Element are unsupported (new lines 124-132).
conflicts: Cross-link November overview lines 76-92 and May acceptance full-only lines 194, 804, 1055. Retain the dated integration detail and warn that the November selector gives no route/version proof. Date the fixed fee, 3DS rates, branding recommendation and prior plain-language categories.
source_assessments.reason: The November overview materially expands payment and post-payment behavior; the existing May-derived summary also contains a supported-country count error and previously compressed scope.

answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay documents a single-use card wallet for Denmark and Finland customers using DKK, EUR, NOK or SEK, with 29 listed business locations, eligible merchant/platform models and a converted minimum based on payout settlement currency. App approval triggers an underlying card payment, with immediate confirmation distinct from standard payout and browser return (new raw lines 9-64 and new raw lines 181-201). Manual partial capture is final and releases the remainder; further capture and overcapture are unsupported. Refund and dispute state follow card rails and issuer rules (new raw lines 66-122). The Payment Element is supported, while Express Checkout Element and Payment Method Messaging Element are unsupported (new raw lines 124-132). Checkout Sessions and PaymentIntents are listed, with SetupIntents, `setup_future_usage` and off-session payments unsupported (new raw lines 143-148). For Stripe front-end products, enable MobilePay in Dashboard Payment methods (old raw lines 102-115 and new raw lines 209-213). For Connect, May documents enabling MobilePay in Payment methods for connected accounts with full Dashboard access. Both captures say to verify `capabilities.mobilepay_payments` is `active` through the Accounts API or webhooks. November explicitly directs a Capabilities API request for connected accounts without full Dashboard access. The request does not establish activation (old raw lines 125-129 and new raw lines 149-151). The May product capture already described the wallet, existing manual capture, card refunds/disputes and Connect, but lacked a partial capture rule (old raw lines 8-52 and old raw lines 117-137). source-stripe-mobilepay.md preserves those fundamentals, miscounts the merchant list as 30 (old raw lines 58-86), and needs November capture, settlement, eligibility and outcome qualifications.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay, the reorganized customer walkthrough and navigation preserve desktop phone/push and mobile redirect (old raw lines 88-115 and new raw lines 181-213). The product overview adds substantive final partial-capture, refund/dispute, API and descriptor detail (new raw lines 66-151 and new raw lines 203-207). Cross-link May's full-only capture language in the separate acceptance guide at lines 194, 804 and 1055 with the November overview's final partial capture, remainder release and no second capture (new raw lines 76-92). Keep Checkout Session versus direct PaymentIntent configuration and the historical authentication window distinct from capture eligibility; the November acceptance selector gives no API version, platform or route body confirmation. A return, approval or authorization does not verify capture, refund completion or payout. In source-stripe-mobilepay.md retain May's Connect charge routes, estimated 3DS rates, fixed 35 DKK fee and icon recommendation as dated (old raw lines 117-129, old raw lines 143-160 and old raw lines 183-214). November qualifies active Danish merchant fees, Visa/Dankort routing, and issuer descriptor display (new raw lines 161-175 and new raw lines 203-207). Numerical omissions do not establish a price change or expanded eligibility.
